title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Pages 26-29 of these notes recapitulate the 'données de déploiement' (unfolding data) of a stratified space indexed by a finite poset I. The data are: spaces Σ_i (the 'deployed' strata, i.e. stratum i with open tubular neighbourhoods of the lower strata removed, a compact manifold with corners in the smooth case); spaces Σ_ij for i<j, closed in Σ_j via b_ij (the boundary piece of Σ_j lying over stratum i); and maps s_ij: Σ_ij → Σ_i (the link-bundle projections). The previous page imposes three conditions: (a) b_ij is a closed embedding; (b) Σ_ik ∩ Σ_jk = ∅ if i, j are incomparable; (c) for i<j<k, Σ_ijk := Σ_ik ∩ Σ_jk equals s_jk^{-1}(Σ_ij), giving a hexagon with two cartesian squares and s_ik = s_ij∘s_jk on Σ_ijk.

This page adds two conditions and then reformulates the whole structure.

(d) The inclusions Σ_ji ↪ Σ_i (j<i) are 'bordantes', i.e. inclusions of boundary pieces. Fix x ∈ Σ_i and set I_{<i,x} := {j<i | x ∈ Σ_ji}; by (b) this set is totally ordered. The Σ_ji with j ∈ I_{<i,x} must be mutually transversal boundary subspaces at x. So Σ_i is a 'manifold with corners' in a topological sense, and the codimension of the corner at x is |I_{<i,x}|, a chain in I.

(e) Each s_ij: Σ_ij → Σ_i is transversal to the transversal system of boundary inclusions b_ki: Σ_ki → Σ_i (k<i). Equivalently, the boundary faces of the link bundle Σ_ij are the pull-backs of the faces of the base. This is the compatibility of fibrations with corners familiar from 'iterated fibration structures'.

Global reformulation. Put Σ = ⊔_i Σ_i and Σ^(1) = ⊔_{i<j} Σ_ij, with s, b: Σ^(1) → Σ. Then conditions a)-c) say the following:
- (s,b): Σ^(1) → Σ×Σ is injective.
- Its image is the graph of a strict order relation on Σ. Here y' < y means y ∈ Σ_ji and y' = s_ji(y).
- The obvious map φ: Σ → I is strictly increasing.
- For each x ∈ Σ_i, the induced map Σ_{<x} → I_{<i} is injective, with image I_{<i,x}.
- Σ_{<x} is totally ordered (this is the reformulation of (b)).

So the deployment is a 'topological strict poset' Σ over I whose lower sets are chains. The next page shows where this is heading: a topological category with s fibrant, whose π_0 gives the (pre)ordered index set. The aim is to free the theory from the auxiliary poset I and to see the stratified space as reconstructible from this topological poset/category.

Why it matters. This is Grothendieck's 'théorème de déploiement' programme from Esquisse §5-6: to replace a (tame) stratified space by combinatorial-topological data made of manifolds with corners and proper fibrations, from which the space is recovered by gluing (mapping cylinders / cones).
errors: Minor gap: the claim that 'a) b) c) signify' the order-theoretic conditions captures only their set-theoretic content. The topological content is not encoded by 'injective with image a graph of a strict order'. That content is: closedness of b_ij, (s,b) being a homeomorphism onto its image, and the cartesian squares being cartesian as spaces. It would require e.g. b restricted to each component to be a closed embedding.

Verification of the reformulation, which works. Transitivity follows from c): if z ∈ Σ_jk and s_jk(z) ∈ Σ_ij, then z ∈ Σ_ijk ⊂ Σ_ik and s_ik(z) = s_ij(s_jk(z)). Antisymmetry follows from φ being strictly increasing. Total order of Σ_{<x} follows from b). Injectivity of (s,b) holds because b_ij are embeddings and different i give targets in different Σ_i.
The word 'immédiates' written near the relation is misleading. Σ^(1) contains all relations i<j, not only immediate successors; nothing on the page restricts to covering relations.
Indexing of Σ_ij vs Σ_ji is used inconsistently between pages, but meaning is clear: Σ_ji ⊂ Σ_i for j<i.

ideas.what: Unfolding (déploiement) of a stratified space into a poset-indexed system of manifolds with corners Σ_i, boundary pieces Σ_ij ⊂ Σ_j and link fibrations s_ij: Σ_ij → Σ_i satisfying a hexagonal cartesian compatibility
ideas.modern_name: Resolution/unfolding of Thom-Mather stratified spaces into manifolds with (fibred) corners; iterated fibration structures; unzipping
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom-Mather control data (1969-70); Verona 'resolution' (1984); Brasselet-Hector-Saralegi unfolding (1992); Albin-Leichtnam-Mazzeo-Piazza (2012); Ayala-Francis-Tanaka unzipping (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 sketches the 'théorème de déploiement' informally; the precise axioms are not published

ideas.what: Condition that at each point the boundary pieces through x are mutually transversal and indexed by a chain I_{<i,x} of the poset (corner codimension = chain length)
ideas.modern_name: Manifold with corners whose boundary hypersurfaces are indexed by strata, with faces meeting only for comparable strata (⟨k⟩-manifold / fibred corners)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jänich, Melrose (manifolds with corners); ALMP for fibred corners

ideas.what: Transversality of the link fibrations s_ij to the corner system of the base (faces of Σ_ij pulled back from faces of Σ_i)
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility condition of an iterated fibration structure / boundary fibration structure

ideas.what: Repackaging the deployment data as a single space Σ = ⊔Σ_i with a 'topological strict order' Σ^(1) ⊂ Σ×Σ, a strictly increasing φ: Σ → I, and lower sets Σ_{<x} that are chains mapping injectively to I. This leads (next page) to topological categories with fibrant source map whose π_0 gives the poset
ideas.modern_name: Poset/category object in Top modelling a stratified space; precursor of exit-path topological categories and stratified homotopy hypothesis
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson/Treumann (exit paths), Lurie (Higher Algebra A.6), Ayala-Francis-Tanaka, Haine, Nand-Lal-Woolf

missed.claim: A complete axiomatization, circa 1981-82, of the 'unfolded' form of a stratified space. It consists of manifolds-with-corners Σ_i, boundary pieces indexed by chains of the stratification poset, and proper link fibrations transversal to the corner system, glued by cartesian hexagons. This is essentially the later 'resolution into manifolds with fibred corners / iterated fibration structures' (Verona, Brasselet-Hector-Saralegi, ALMP) and AFT's unzipping, formulated purely topologically.
missed.quote: les Σ_ji (j ∈ I_{<i}) sont des sous-espaces bords de Σ_i mutuellement transversaux en x ... Σ_ij → Σ_i est transversal au système transversal des morphismes bordants
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck's déploiement anticipates the resolution/unzipping technology now central to analysis on stratified spaces and to conically smooth stratified spaces. It is relevant to crediting and to a purely topological (non-smooth) version of these theories.

missed.claim: Encoding the deployment as a topological strict poset over I with chain-like lower sets, then generalizing to a topological category with fibrant source map. This links unfolded stratified spaces to category objects in spaces, i.e. to what later became exit-path ∞-categories and the stratified homotopy hypothesis. The link here is made at the level of the resolved (corner) model rather than the singular space.
missed.quote: (s,b): Σ^(1) → Σ×Σ est inj. et a comme image le graphe d'une relation d'ordre stricte ... Σ_{<x} est totalement ordonné
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a direct model of exit-path categories via unzipped data. AFT do something similar, but Grothendieck's 'topological poset with chain lower-sets' formulation and the fibrant-source condition give a concrete point-set model. Its comparison with Lurie/Haine models seems not explicitly worked out in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: The page gives precise axioms for Grothendieck's 'déploiement', which is only sketched in Esquisse. It anticipates resolution-to-fibred-corners and unzipping constructions developed later by others, and points toward topological-category models of stratifications. The individual ingredients are, however, now standard in the literature, so this is a notable unpublished precursor rather than an unknown result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Les Σ_j ↪ Σ_ji sont bordantes' should read 'Les Σ_ji ↪ Σ_i sont bordantes, et si x ∈ Σ_i, les Σ_ji ∋ x'.
Definition of I_{<i,x}: should be {j ∈ I | j<i, Σ_ji ∋ x} (the Σ_ji, not Σ_j).
Condition e) reads approximately: 'Σ_ij --s_ij--> Σ_i est transversal [au] système transversal des morphismes bordants b_ki: Σ_ki → Σ_i'.
'Si on pose' should be read as 'Si on pose' / 'Lorsqu'on pose'. 'dans les conditions a) b) c)' means 'alors les conditions a) b) c) signifient que'.
'φ: Σ^* ? → I' is just 'φ: Σ → I' (the obvious induced map, 'induite évidente').
The last line reads 'l'application induite φ: Σ_{<x} → I_{<i} (i=φ(x)) est injective, ainsi que Σ_{<x} est totalement ordonné'. The '∐' is not present.
